Lab 0: Web Development Basics

Lab 0: Web Development Basics

CMSC471: Introduction to Information Visualization (Spring 2026)

This lab introduces you to the fundamental concepts of web development. We’ll build a simple webpage that will serve as the foundation for future D3.js labs. Each step is explained in detail to ensure you understand not just what to do, but why you’re doing it. For those who have web programming experience, this lab will also help you refresh your memory and skills.

By the end of this lab, you will be able to:

  • Create and organize a web project folder structure
  • Write basic HTML, CSS, and JavaScript code.
  • Use browser developer tools for debugging
  • Include external libraries in your web projects
  • Verify your development environment is ready for D3.js

Grade (3% of total course grade): This lab is graded out of 30 points. You may submit your lab in person during the lab session on Wednesday, Feb 4, 2026 or Wednesday, Feb 11, 2026, or during any office hours.

The final submission deadline is Thursday, Feb 12, 2026 at 6:00 PM (ET).

Part 0: For beginners

If you feel you don’t know javascript at all, you can first try to finish this lab and then learn the syntax after the lab. The suggested readings include:

One of the tutorials for understanding Javascript syntax:

  • Learning Javascript as a Python Developer
  • Transitioning from Java to JavaScript

One of the tutorials for understanding HTML/CSS syntax:

  • HTML and CSS for Python Developers
  • JavaScript and HTML DOM

Although you don’t need them for this lab, I highly recommend reading Arrow Function Expressions (at least the first half). This is good for understanding things like these:

() => expression

param => expression

(param) => expression

(param1, paramN) => expression

() => {
  statements
}

param => {
  statements
}

(param1, paramN) => {
  statements
}

Part 1: Development tools

Now let’s get started.

Text editor (VS Code)

Visual Studio Code (VS Code) is a powerful, free text editor that makes writing code easier. It provides:

  • Syntax highlighting (makes code more readable)
  • Auto-completion (helps prevent typing errors)
  • Built-in terminal (run commands easily)
  • Extensions (add extra features)

How to install:

  1. Go to https://code.visualstudio.com/
  2. Download the version for your operating system
  3. Run the installer
  4. Open VS Code after installation

Essential and optional extensions:

  1. Live Server
    • Why: Automatically reloads your page when you save changes
    • How: Click Extensions icon (puzzle piece on the left side or search in Help) → Search “Live Server” → Install
  2. HTML CSS support (optional)
    • Why: Helps write HTML and CSS with suggestions
    • How: Same process as Live Server
Install live server

Web browser (Chrome)

Google Chrome is our recommended browser for development. Chrome provides strong compatibility with modern web features and consistent rendering.

How to install:

  1. Visit https://www.google.com/chrome; Download and install
  2. Learn to open and close Developer Tools:
    • Windows: Press F12 or Ctrl+Shift+I
    • Mac: Press Cmd+Option+I
    • View → Developer → Developer Tool
    • Press the shortcuts again to close it

Part 2: Project structure

Web Project organization

We’ll create a specific folder structure for our web project. Good organization makes files easy to find, follows industry standards, makes collaboration easier, and helps prevent errors.

Creating your project

Step-by-Step Instructions: First, create a folder for this course CMSC471. Within this folder,

  1. Create main project folder:

    lab0/

  2. Create subfolders: Inside lab0, create:

    css/    (for styling files)
js/     (for JavaScript files)

    Why separate folders?

    • Keeps code organized by purpose
    • Makes it easier to maintain
    • Industry standard practice

  3. Create required files (placeholders):

    index.html    (main HTML file)  
css/styles.css   (styling)
js/script.js     (JavaScript code)

    Use exact names (case sensitive!)

Part 3: Writing code

HTML (index.html)

HTML is the structure of your webpage.

Understanding each part:

<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
    <!-- Meta information goes here -->
    <meta charset="utf-8">
    <!-- Ensures proper character encoding -->
    
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
    <!-- Makes your page mobile-friendly -->
    
    <title>Lab 0 - Web Dev Setup</title>
    <!-- Shows in browser tab -->
    
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/styles.css">
    <!-- Connects your CSS file -->
</head>
<body>
    <div class="container">
        <!-- Main content container -->
        <h1>Hello, Web Development!</h1>
        <!-- Main heading -->
        
        <p class="intro">This is my first lab setup.</p>
        <!-- Paragraph with a class for styling -->
        
        <div id="content">
            <!-- Content section with ID for JavaScript -->
            <p>I'm ready to learn D3.js!</p>
        </div>
    </div>

    <!-- Load libraries before your code -->
    <script src="https://d3js.org/d3.v7.min.js"></script>
    <script src="js/script.js"></script>
</body>
</html>

Key concepts:

  1. HTML Tags (e.g. <body> , <div>)
    • Always have opening (e.g., <body>) and closing tags (e.g., <body/>)(mostly)
    • Nested them properly (like folders)
  2. Attributes
    • class: For CSS styling
    • id: For unique elements
    • src: For file sources
    • href: For hyperlinks

CSS (styles.css)

CSS controls how your webpage looks.

Understanding the code:

/* Reset default styles */
* {
    font-family: Arial, sans-serif;
    max-width: 800px;
    margin: 0 auto;
    padding: 20px;
}
/* Why: Creates consistent starting point */

/* Typography styling */
h1 {
    color: #2c3e50;  
}

/* Class selector */
.intro {
    color: #34495e;
    font-size: 18px;
}

/* ID selector */
#content {
    margin-top: 20px;
    padding: 20px;
    background-color: #f7f9fc;
    border-radius: 5px;  /* Rounded corners */
}

Key concepts:

  1. Selectors
    • Element selectors (h1, p)
    • Class selectors (.intro)
    • ID selectors (#content)
  2. Properties
    • color: text color
    • margin: Space outside element
    • padding: Space inside element
    • font-family: text style

JavaScript (script.js)

JavaScript makes your webpage interactive.

Understanding the code:

// Verify script is working
console.log('Script loaded successfully!');
/* Why: Immediate feedback in console */

// Select HTML element
const heading = document.querySelector('h1');
/* Why: Gets reference to h1 tag */

// Add interactive behavior
heading.style.cursor = 'pointer';
/* Why: Shows element is clickable */

// Event listener
heading.addEventListener('click', function() {
    this.style.color = getRandomColor();
});
/* Why: Makes heading change color when clicked */

// Check D3.js
console.log('D3 Version:', d3?.version || 'D3 not loaded');
/* Why: Confirms D3 library is available */

// Helper function
function getRandomColor() {
    const letters = '0123456789ABCDEF';
    let color = '#';
    for (let i = 0; i < 6; i++) {
        color += letters[Math.floor(Math.random() * 16)];
    }
    return color;
}
/* Why: Creates random color for interaction */

Part 4: Testing your code

Using live server

  1. Right-click index.html in VS Code
  2. Select Open with Live Server (or the little Go Live) at the bottom right of your screen.
  3. Your page should automatically open in Chrome (or your default browser)

Using developer tools

  1. Open Chrome Developer Tools (View → Developer → Developer Tool; or use shortcuts)
  2. Explore each tab:
    • Elements: See HTML structure (Try: click on the cursor icon at the left top, and then hover over each elemnt on the page)
    • Console: Check JavaScript output
    • Sources: Find your files
    • Network: See file loading
Results of Lab 0

Common Issues and Solutions

  1. Page not loading
    • Check file names (case sensitive!)
    • Verify all files are in the correct folders
    • Check Live Server is running
  2. Styles not working
    • Check CSS file path
    • Verify CSS syntax
    • Look for typos in class names
  3. JavaScript not working
    • Check Console for errors
    • Verify script tags are present
    • Check file paths
